paragraphs: Here's what this whole passage is about, friend. God's people weren't hurting because He had gone quiet. The LORD says it is because they "have forsaken My law, which I set before them" and followed "the stubbornness of their hearts" (Jeremiah 9:13-14). The wailing, the empty fields and the long road away all trace back to the same spot: a people who stopped listening to Him.

Then the LORD turns to what people lean on when they feel safe. "Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor the strong man in his strength, nor the wealthy man in his riches" (Jeremiah 9:23). Brains, muscles and a fat bank account are the three things everybody brags about, and the LORD sets all three down at once. I have a lot of respect for a good brag, so listen to the better one: "that he understands and knows Me, that I am the LORD, who exercises loving devotion, justice and righteousness on the earth" (Jeremiah 9:24).

So what does that mean for you today? Knowing the LORD is the thing worth holding on to, and it's more than a fact you keep in your head. The passage ends by saying the whole house of Israel is "uncircumcised in heart" (Jeremiah 9:26), which tells me God cares about what's going on inside us, not just what looks right outside. Let Him have your heart, and when you want to brag, brag about Him. THAT'S the brag that holds up.
